title: Reproducing Fukuda et al. 1992: trap density and charge of rapid thermal oxides

sample.paper: “5 in. n-type, 5-8 Ω cm, Si(100) wafers”
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si100; DOPING: n_type_5_8_ohm_cm (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.paper: “cleaned with a H2SO4-H2O2 mixture, then with 1% HF acid, and finally rinsed in deionized water”
n+ polysilicon gate, 350 nm, doped to 4×10^20 cm⁻³; gate area 2.704×10⁻³ cm²
sample.ours: not in our sample; the gate's deposition and doping are RUNs

sample.paper: “typically in the range of 4-10 nm”; uniformity ±3%; method not stated
sample.note: No thickness is given per oxidation time. Figure 2's points are paired with Figure 3's here by their trap densities; that pairing is ours.

sample.paper: “More than 40 wafers subjected to different processing conditions were fabricated and tested.”

history.item: H2SO4-H2O2, then 1% HF, then deionized water
history.paper: “The wafers were cleaned with a H2SO4-H2O2 mixture, then with 1% HF acid, and finally rinsed in deionized water.”
history.ours: CLEAN: sulfuric_peroxide_HF on the sample; no program reads it
history.note: Times and temperatures of the baths not stated.

history.item: Loaded “immediately” into the lamp-heated RTP chamber
history.paper: “After the cleaning, these wafers were immediately loaded into a RTP chamber equipped with tungsten-halogen lamp heaters and an oil-free vacuum pumping system.”
history.note: Chamber pressure, pump-down and purge before the oxygen is let in: not stated.

history.item: Lamp heat-up to 1000 °C (assumed: 10 s, in the evacuated chamber)
history.ours: RUN HeatUp DURATION 10 TEMP 25->1000 AMBIENT vacuum PROFILE settling TAU 2
history.note: The paper gives no ramp rate, and does not say whether the stated oxidation time includes the heat-up. Ours: a settling profile (PROFILE settling, TAU 2 s) reaching the hold temperature in 10 s, in vacuum, so that no oxide grows before the stated time. Written in vacuum, not oxygen, also because the trap-density program takes the oxidation temperature from the first oxygen step's start temperature (see the variant).

history.item: Rapid thermal oxidation, dry O2, 1000 °C, 10 s
history.paper: “The SiO2 films were formed in dry oxygen ambient at 1000-1200 °C for 1-100 s by irradiation with infrared light.”; the time is on the axis of Figure 3
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 10 TEMP 1000->1000 AMBIENT dry_O2

history.item: Lamps off: cool from 1000 °C to 300 °C (assumed: 30 s, settling)
history.ours: RUN Cool DURATION 30 TEMP 1000->300 AMBIENT dry_O2 PROFILE settling TAU 6
history.note: Neither the cooling rate nor the gas during cooling is stated. Ours: the oxygen left on, PROFILE settling with TAU 6 s, about 130 °C/s at the start. Below 350 °C the fixed-charge program's exchange with oxygen is frozen (T_freeze, a hypothesis), so the end temperature is not searched.

history.item: LPCVD polysilicon, 350 nm, at 620 °C (silane written as nitrogen; time ours)
history.paper: “350-nm-thick polysilicon layers were deposited by conventional low-pressure chemical-vapor deposition (LPCVD) at 620 °C”
history.ours: RUN PolyDeposition DURATION 2400 TEMP 620->620 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: The temperature is stated; the time is not (40 min is ours, about 9 nm/min) and the silane cannot be written: the language has no SiH4. The oxide is capped by the silicon as it grows, so nitrogen is written: no program here reads a deposition.

history.item: Phosphorus doping of the gate to 4×10^20 cm⁻³ at 900 °C (time and gas ours)
history.paper: “and then doped with phosphorous to 4x10^20 cm-3 at 900 °C”
history.ours: RUN GateDoping DURATION 1800 TEMP 900->900 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: 900 °C is stated; the time, the dopant source and the gas are not. The gate oxide is under 350 nm of silicon, so the gas does not reach it; nitrogen is written. This step comes after every anneal the paper studies and is hotter than the 500 °C anneals.

history.item: Cool after doping (assumed: 5 min to 300 °C, nitrogen)
history.ours: RUN DopingCool DURATION 300 TEMP 900->300 AMBIENT inert_N2 PROFILE settling TAU 60
history.note: Ours. Without it the history would end at 900 °C.

history.paper: “Finally, gate electrodes with an area of 2.704x10-3 cm2 were defined by conventional photolithography.”
history.note: No sinter or forming-gas anneal is mentioned after the gate.

history.paper: “High-frequency (1 MHz) and quasistatic capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurements were performed to determine the density of interface trap states Dit and fixed oxide charge density Nss.”
history.note: “there was indeed a certain degree of device-to-device scattering (< 10%)”; “only typical or representative results are reported”.

history.item: Ramp and cooling of the RTP
history.ours: RUN HeatUp 10 s (vacuum) and RUN Cool 30 s (oxygen), both settling, both VARY duration

history.paper: not stated, except the vacuum anneal: “rapidly pumping the oxygen gas after the oxidation and, simultaneously, the temperature was decreased to 900 °C”
history.ours: vacuum: in situ (RUN PumpDown); deuterium and argon: a separate heat-up from room temperature (ours)

history.paper: D2 “as a readily traceable isotope that simulates hydrogen chemistry”
history.note: The language has no D2; written as hydrogen.

history.ours: not compared: no program reports hydrogen in the oxide
